newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines 1996 unmilled rice output seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Philippines 1996 unmilled rice output seen higher.

text.p: Philippine unmilled rice output is expected to rise to 12 million tonnes this year from 10.5 million tonnes in 1995, the Department of Agriculture said on Wednesday.

"The target seems attainable based on initial harvest reports from key rice growing areas after the government launched early this year its rice productivitity campaign," agriculture undersecretary Domingo Panganiban said in a phone interview.
Philippine officials have said the total area planted to rice has increased this year, partly as a result of a government credit programme to encourage output.

The state National Food Authority (NFA) said it has earmarked 3.5 billion pesos to buy unmilled rice and another 390 million pesos to buy corn at premium prices from farmers as part of the government's campaign to shore up the country's grains harvests.
"The food agency is targeting to buy through direct procurement 440,000 tonnes of (unmilled rice) and 60,000 tonnes of corn for 1996," NFA acting administrator Joemari Gerochi said in a statement.
Unmilled rice prices dropped to an average of 8.73 per kg nationwide from 9.22 per kg three weeks ago with the start of the harvest season, the NFA said.
NFA said it buys unmilled rice at eight pesos per kg from farmers and 8.50 per kg from cooperatives.
It also buys corn at six pesos per kg from farmers and 6.50 per kg from cooperatives.
The government has imported 840,000 tonnes of rice and 250,000 tonnes of corn since the start of the year.
